Help with costs, rides and medicines

Cancer care can be hard to afford and hard to get to. These free programs help many patients. Ask your clinic’s social worker or financial counselor too — that is their job.

Rides to treatment

  • Medi-Cal ridesIf you have Medi-Cal, rides to covered medical visits are included. Call the member services number on your Medi-Cal plan card to schedule, a few days ahead. How Medi-Cal rides work
  • American Cancer Society Road To RecoveryFree rides to cancer appointments by volunteer drivers, where available. Call several days before your visit. 1-800-227-2345

Health coverage

  • Medi-CalCalifornia’s free or low-cost health coverage. You can apply any time of year. Apply at BenefitsCal
  • Covered CaliforniaHealth plans with help paying the cost, based on income. coveredca.com

Paying for medicines

  • Ask about patient assistanceMost companies that make cancer medicines have programs that lower the cost or give the medicine free to people who qualify. Ask your clinic or pharmacist to help you apply.
  • NeedyMedsA free directory of medicine assistance programs and discount cards. needymeds.org
  • Patient Advocate FoundationFree case managers who help with insurance problems, medical bills and co-pay assistance. patientadvocate.org

Food, housing, bills and more

  • 211 LADial 2-1-1 any time, in English or Spanish, for food, housing, utilities and local services. 211la.org
  • CancerCareFree counseling and support groups by phone or online, and limited financial help. 1-800-813-4673
  • American Cancer Society helplineAnswers and referrals, 24 hours a day, with Spanish-speaking staff. 1-800-227-2345

Tip: tell your care team early if money, work, transportation or immigration worries make treatment hard. There is often help.

General education only; it does not replace advice from your own care team. Program details change, so confirm with each organization. This is Dr. Ehsan’s personal, independent website and has no connection to any of his current or former employers.
